name: MESA
description: Earth’s surface anomaly (ESA), encompassing natural disasters and man-made incidents, poses significant threats to global safety and security, necessitating rapid detection and effective response. The integration of remote sensing (RS) and deep learning (DL), coupled with the availability of many very high resolution (VHR) datasets, have significantly advanced research about ESA detection, facilitating the Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Response (HADR). However, the inherent randomness and unpredictability of ESA presents challenges for comprehensive data collection, resulting in existing datasets that fall short in terms of data diversity, distribution, and scale to meet the immediate RS demands. To bridge these gaps, we introduce MESA, a large-scale benchmark dataset specially designed for multi-class Earth’s surface anomaly (MESA) detection in single VHR images, aimed at enhancing the generalizability and robustness of DL models across diverse classes and real-world conditions. MESA comprises 20,351 samples of 1024 × 1024 pixels with sub-meter resolutions ranging from 0.2m to 1m, covering 12 anomaly classes associated with 82 events worldwide. The benchmark experiments demonstrate that the graph neural networks (GNN)-based L2S-Net, which explicitly learns relationships among ground objects, outperforms classical vision models while maintaining a lightweight architecture. MESA provides a robust foundation for advancing ESA research, paving the way for the development of more accurate, scalable, and real-time systems to address critical global challenges.
reputation: Newly published remote sensing benchmark (2025); of interest to earth-observation researchers but not yet widely adopted across the broader ML community.
notes: Very-high-resolution imagery can introduce geographic and sensor biases; likely class imbalance and high annotation cost. Not an LLM benchmark and may contain proprietary imagery sources—careful license review required.
